calls.title: Unity<>GrowthBook - Configurations Session
calls.summary: The discussion revolved around the team's hierarchical, attribute-driven configuration platform which manages feature flags through a parent-child tree model, allowing granularity in customer configuration with overrides. Challenges related to version-dependent overrides complicating maintenance and user experience visibility were identified, alongside strict customer segmentation practices to prevent configuration bleed. The integration strategy for GrowthBook was reviewed, outlining how products would be structured as projects and customers as environments, with challenges on inheritance and rule sharing. Additionally, validation enhancements like JSON schema support and approval workflows were discussed to ensure quality control. The team also explored simulation capabilities and the need for improved holistic views on user experience changes across features, outlining their next steps and collaboration efforts.
calls.keywords: Configuration Hierarchy, Feature Flags, Environment Model, JSON Schema Validation, Approval Workflow, GrowthBook Simulation

calls.title: Unity<>GrowthBook - Configurations best practices
calls.summary: The team discussed the successful migration of multiple customer environments, ensuring configurations align to maintain production consistency. Key issues included gaps in boolean attribute handling during simulations, impacting testing efficiency. It was noted that the lack of API support for custom hooks limits automation, although JSON schema validations cover most scenarios. The group explored strategies for isolated developer environments, suggesting separate GrowthBook instances for testing with periodic syncing of configurations. They requested a trial extension to thoroughly evaluate premium features, showing positive engagement with the ongoing collaboration despite some identified gaps in the simulation user experience.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, migration, archetypes, simulation, environment inheritance, rate limits
